source_inspection_notes: Read rtlo.py in full: its regex (`re.compile('.*\u202e.*')`) checks ONLY for U+202E (Right-to-Left Override). EthTrust's requirement names NINE characters: U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2029, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+202D, U+202E. Slither covers 1 of 9.

derivation_trace.ethtrust_phrase: any of the Unicode Direction Control Characters U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2029, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+202D, or U+202E
derivation_trace.analyzer_behavior: Regex-matches only U+202E in the raw source bytes.
uncovered_cases: the other 8 named characters -- U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2029, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+202D -- entirely uncovered
derivation_trace.final_classification: PARTIAL_MATCH -- a real, substantial coverage gap (8/9 characters), not a technicality. Trivially fixable: rtlo.py's own regex approach generalizes directly to a 9-character alternation, since EthTrust names the exact codepoints -- no interpretation needed, purely mechanical extension of an existing, already-reused technique.
